children: Rohit Srivastava, Founder and Strategist at Indiacharts.com and Strike Money, retains his Nifty target of 35,000 over the next 18 months, while cautioning that a short-term correction after the recent rally could offer investors another entry point.
"If you've gone up 10% or more, you can always give back 2-3% before you move higher. So, I think we should remain prepared for that," Srivastava said.

He expects the broader market trend to remain positive despite signs of fading momentum in the near term and any decline to be temporary. Sectors such as banking, automobiles and real estate will continue to lead the next phase of the rally.

The weakness in global markets and broad-based selling in US equities is likely to weigh on sentiment and trigger a pullback in Indian markets. However, he believes such a move would provide a fresh buying opportunity rather than signal a change in trend.

Srivastava said there are no technical signs of a reversal yet on Bank Nifty despite the strong rally in banking stocks. The index could continue to make new highs over the next few days. If it corrects, the 60,300 level could offer support, as a recent price gap remains unfilled there.
He added that if a correction occurs, the index could find support around the 60,300 level, where a recent gap remains unfilled.
He expects interest rate-sensitive sectors to remain market leaders. Banking stocks remain his preferred play, while autos and real estate also stand to benefit as bond yields soften.
Srivastava said the bond market is already signalling that yields may have peaked, even if there is one more interest rate hike in India or the US.
He also sees potential opportunities emerging in commodities if the US dollar weakens, although he is waiting for confirmation before turning positive on the sector.

title: Rohit Srivastava retains 35,000 Nifty target for next 18 months, sees dips as buying opportunities
